chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Itikaaf (seclusion) is not valid in less than three days, and whoever performs Itikaaf should Fast; and it is befitting for the one performing Itikaaf that when he does perform Itikaaf, he should stipulate just as the one who wears an Ihraam stipulates.

key_terms.الِاعْتِكَافُ: Itikaaf: Seclusion in a mosque for worship
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Three days: The minimum duration for valid Itikaaf
key_terms.صَامَ: He fasted: The requirement of fasting during Itikaaf
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَ: He should stipulate: To specify the type of ritual via intention
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: He wears Ihraam: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum duration and fasting requirements for Itikaaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the minimum duration for Itikaaf as three days, a ruling that distinguishes it from the shorter, voluntary seclusion often practiced in other traditions. It emphasizes that fasting is an integral condition for the validity of the seclusion and requires the mu'takif to specify their intention regarding the type of Itikaaf, mirroring the precise stipulations made by pilgrims entering Ihraam. This highlights the structured, ritualistic nature of Itikaaf within Shia jurisprudence, linking it closely to the broader framework of worship and intentionality.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Itikaaf does not take place in less than three days, and the one who performs Itikaaf should Fast; and it is befitting for the one performing Itikaaf that when he does perform Itikaaf, he should stipulate just as the one who wears an Ihraam stipulates’ (if its for Umra or Hajj).
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
An Ttikaf for less than three days is not valid. One who is in Ttikaf must also fast and it is proper for one in Ttikaf to set a condition as a person in the state of ’Ihram does.’”
